title: Freshness: Reference table stream, debounced wire-snapshot schedule, incremental listing re-render
description:
Phase 4 of the `wire` epic: curation changes reach the public pages by themselves.

## Goal
A `wire` backend plugin: a DynamoDB stream on the Reference table (and the Message table, consumed by the threads task later) feeds a small trigger Lambda that debounces and schedules the `wire-snapshot` projection task. An optional periodic rule is the safety net. Chosen over per-accept re-projection (bursts), periodic-only (stale and wasteful) and client-side JSON (no SEO, no twins); reasons in the epic.

## Files to create
- `amplify/plugins/wire/papyrus.plugin.ts`: `PapyrusPlugin<WireConfig>` (manifest `{name: "wire", contract: 1, models: [], mutations: [], guest: {mutations: []}, newsroomPanels: [], staticAssets: []}`); `resolveConfig` reads `projection.json` `wire.freshness` through the existing public-settings path (`publicSettings`), with `debounceSeconds` default 300, `intervalHours` default none, `purge` default false. `wire(backend, config, context)`:
  1. `cfnTables.Reference.streamSpecification = {streamViewType: NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES}` (copy the Message lookup pattern from `amplify/site-backend.ts` lines 217-230, including the fallback search by table name).
  2. `new NodejsFunction`/Python function `wireTrigger` (Python 3.12, arm64, 256 MB, 30 s) with `DynamoEventSource(referenceTable, {startingPosition: TRIM_HORIZON, batchSize: 100, maxBatchingWindow: 10 s, bisectBatchOnError: true, retryAttempts: 2, filters: [FilterCriteria.filter({dynamodb: {NewImage: {curationStatus: {S: FilterRule.exists()}}}})]})`.
  3. Scheduler role + `scheduler:CreateSchedule` on `schedule/default/papyrus-wire-snapshot-*` + `iam:PassRole`, exactly as `reader-steering/papyrus.plugin.ts` does for `papyrus-reader-snapshot-*`.
  4. Environment on the trigger: `PAPYRUS_WIRE_SNAPSHOT_FUNCTION_ARN` (content-actions), `PAPYRUS_WIRE_SCHEDULER_ROLE_ARN`, `PAPYRUS_WIRE_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS`, `PAPYRUS_PROJECTION_LOCK_TABLE` (reuse the projection lock table for the debounce item; grant `dynamodb:PutItem/DeleteItem` on it).
  5. If `intervalHours` is set: `events.Rule` with `Schedule.rate(Duration.hours(n))` targeting content-actions with `{"projectionTask": {"task": "wire-snapshot"}}`, `retryAttempts: 0` (copy the reader-steering rule).
- `amplify/plugins/wire/function/handler.py`: `handler(event, context)`: for each record, skip unless `eventName` is INSERT/MODIFY and one of `curationStatus`, `feedStateKey`, `predictionSortKey`, `versionState`, `title`, `curationSectionId` differs between OLD and NEW images (REMOVE counts as a change); if anything changed, `claim_slot()` = conditional `PutItem` `{"pk": "wire-debounce#<bucket>", "lockedUntil": now + debounce, "expiresAt": ...}` with `attribute_not_exists(pk) OR lockedUntil <= :now`; on success `create_schedule(Name=f"papyrus-wire-snapshot-{lockedUntil}", ScheduleExpression=at(...), FlexibleTimeWindow OFF, ActionAfterCompletion DELETE, Target content-actions with Input `{"projectionTask": {"task": "wire-snapshot"}}`, RetryPolicy 0)`; on `ConflictException` ignore; on any other error release the slot. Port `claim_snapshot_slot`/`release_snapshot_slot` from `amplify/plugins/reader-steering/function/handler.py`.
- `amplify/plugins/wire/function/handler_test.py` (unit tests with stubbed boto3).
- `features_backend/wire-freshness.feature` + steps (pure-Python tests of the change filter, the debounce claim and the schedule name; the CDK wiring is covered by `npx tsc --noEmit` and a synth test if the repo has one for plugins).

## Files to change
- `amplify/plugins/registry.ts` `KNOWN_PLUGINS`: add `wire`.
- `amplify/plugins/wire.ts` (the wiring entry, if plugins are listed there) and `PAPYRUS_PLUGINS` handling: nothing else; `PLUGIN_STATIC_ASSETS["wire"]` is empty.
- `src/papyrus_content/projection/plugins.py`: `PLUGIN_RUNTIME_DIRECTORIES` already has `_data/wire/` from the snapshot task.
- `amplify/functions/content-actions/handler.py`: when `task == "wire-snapshot"`, after `run_wire_snapshot`, if `settings.freshness.purge` call `context.invalidate(keys)` with the written keys (the task already does this; keep the purge in the task, not the handler).
- `docs/wire.md`: freshness section (window, s-maxage reasoning, purge switch, periodic rule).

## Gherkin scenarios (features_backend/wire-freshness.feature)
- "A vote that changes a Reference's curation status schedules one snapshot at the end of the debounce window"
- "Ten accepts inside one window schedule exactly one snapshot"
- "An edit that changes no public field schedules nothing"
- "A failed schedule creation releases the slot so the next change can try again"
- "The snapshot re-renders only the pages that read the changed selection" (shares steps with the snapshot feature)
- "A site with purge off relies on the edge lifetime; a site with purge on invalidates exactly the rewritten keys"
- "A site with an interval set runs the snapshot on that interval even without changes"

## Acceptance checks
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, unit tests, behave green.
- After deploy on Anth.us (needs a Papyrus release + Anth.us version bump + `backend.plugins: ["wire"]`): accept one Reference in newsroom.anth.us, wait debounce + 300 s, reload https://anth.us/newsroom/ and see it. Check CloudWatch for one content-actions `wire-snapshot` invocation per burst.
- Cost note in the PR: expected invocations per day on Anth.us from the last week's curation counts (read-only query), to confirm the window is right; adjust `debounceSeconds` from data, not by guess.

## Dependencies
Depends on: wire snapshot. Blocks: threads (reuses the trigger for the Message table). New scheduled compute: say so in the PR; Ryan approves the deploy as part of the Anth.us version bump.
